en: I am waiting for a bus at the stop.
note: ждать + genitive is the indefinite object and + accusative the definite one — a distinction English marks with a/the, so the prompt can carry the whole of it rather than leaving the learner to guess which case is wanted.

standard: market (an open-air bazaar, the colloquial word)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). база́р is the open-air bazaar and the colloquial word; ры́нок is the standard one. Naming a bazaar in both glosses helped nobody choose.

ru: По сре́дам я хожу́ в бассе́йн.
ru_new: По среда́м я хожу́ в бассе́йн.
note: One sentence spelled two ways. среда's own declension stores pl_dat среда́м, and calendar.yml's copy — the one annotated on that very token — agrees; this copy did not.

en_alt: She used to thank the teacher.
note: The imperfective and its perfective partner shared one prompt. 'She was thanking the teacher' was already listed as an accepted answer here — it is the prompt this sentence should be asking with. The old prompt is NOT kept as an alternate: 'She thanked the teacher' is word for word the perfective partner's own sentence «Она́ поблагодари́ла учи́теля», so accepting it here marks the perfective reading correct for the imperfective and undoes the aspect fix this pass just made. Found by the alternates audit (#599); this stage owns the list, so the removal lands here rather than in alt-removals.jsonl, which runs before it.

en: Don't be nervous, everything will be fine.
note: Repeated беспоко́иться's prompt verbatim. волнова́ться is the agitated, nervous word — as its own «Он волну́ется пе́ред экза́меном» already says — so the prompt says so too.

standard: soon (bookish, shortly after some other event)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). вско́ре is bookish and measured from another event; ско́ро is the everyday word measured from now. 'A short time later' against 'in a short time' was two strings for one definition.

standard: reality (the native, bookish word for how things actually are)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). действи́тельность is the native, bookish word; реа́льность is the everyday borrowing.

standard: to become (colloquial, of a state coming on by itself)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). де́латься is colloquial, of a state coming on by itself; станови́ться is the everyday word.

standard: to achieve (to get what you pressed for, after effort)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). доби́ться is getting what you pressed for, after effort; дости́чь is simply arriving at a level or result. 'To attain through effort' against 'to achieve a goal' read as one idea twice.

standard: to reach (to arrive at a level, point or result)
note: The imperfective of дости́чь, kept in step with it so the pair reads consistently across the drills.

standard: to reach (to arrive at a level or result; a variant of дости́чь)
note: дости́гнуть and дости́чь are variant infinitives of one perfective verb, so the sharpened note above would have rendered an identical spelling prompt for both — spellPromptData guards exactly that. This one names itself the variant.

standard: to reach (to arrive at a level, point or result)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). дости́чь is arriving at a level, point or result, with no implication of struggle; доби́ться is winning it.

'Where are you going?' reads as either verb, and this sentence also blocked the ты/вы annotator from separating «Куда́ ты идёшь?» from «Куда́ вы идёте?». 'Travelling' picks out the by-transport verb and leaves that pair to the annotator.

«Здра́вствуйте, как ва́ши дела́?» commits to вы and this one committed to nothing, so the ты/вы annotator could not separate them. «как твои́ дела́?» is the ordinary informal form and makes the pair parallel; no new machinery needed.

standard: to mean (the everyday word; значит also means so, therefore)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). зна́чить is the everyday word, and «зна́чит» doubles as 'so, therefore'; means-as-denote is означа́ть's job.

standard: truth (the abstract or philosophical truth)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). и́стина is the abstract or philosophical truth; пра́вда is what really happened.

standard: extremely (the everyday intensifier)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). кра́йне is the everyday intensifier; чрезвыча́йно is formal. 'To the highest degree' against 'to a very great degree' distinguished nothing.

standard: creative (a recent borrowing, used of ideas and business)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). креати́вный is the recent English borrowing, at home in ideas and business; тво́рческий is the native word tied to тво́рчество and to art.
да and и are both conjunctions, which the hint builder never uses, so the collision with да's «Купи́ хлеб да молоко́» could only go from the sentence. купи́ть keeps its imperative at token 1.
«Сего́дня мне лу́чше» is the impersonal dative with no verb of feeling in it, so 'Today I am better' both renders it and stops it colliding with «Сего́дня я чу́вствую себя́ лу́чше».
One sentence spelled two ways. год stores sg_loc году́, which is the form в governs here; numerals.yml's copy agrees and this one did not.

en: Put the book on the table.
note: A clone of ча́шка's «Поста́вь ча́шку на стол», and odd Russian besides — a cup is stood, not laid. A book beside «Кни́га на столе́» also gives на its where/whither contrast inside one entry.

ru_new: Надева́й ша́пку, когда́ на у́лице моро́з.
en: Put on a hat when it's freezing outside.
note: Collided with ша́пка's perfective «Наде́нь ша́пку, на у́лице моро́з». The imperfective imperative is the standing instruction — whenever it is freezing — which is the aspect distinction rather than a dodge around it. The annotated token 1 is untouched.

standard: incorrect (untrue or mistaken; also unfaithful)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). неве́рный is untrue or mistaken — and carries the 'unfaithful' sense too; непра́вильный is what breaks a rule.

standard: incorrect (against the rules, the everyday word)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). непра́вильный is the everyday word for what breaks a rule; неве́рный is what is untrue.

standard: to mean (formal, to denote or stand for)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). означа́ть is the formal word, used of signs and terms; зна́чить is everyday.
One sentence spelled two ways. The stress is полице́йский, as полице́йский's own headword and its copy of this sentence both have it.

en: Wait for me at the entrance for a while.
note: Shared a prompt with ждать's «Жди меня́ у вхо́да». подожда́ть is a по- delimitative, and 'for a while' is the convention the corpus already uses for помолча́ть and посиде́ть.

standard: clearly (understood, the hearer has grasped it)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). поня́тно is about the hearer having grasped it; я́сно is about the thing being evident. Both read 'it is clear' before.

standard: truth (the everyday word, what really happened)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). пра́вда is the everyday word for what really happened; и́стина is the abstract truth.

en: Wash your hands before you eat.
note: Three sentences shared 'Wash your hands before eating'. «пре́жде чем есть» is a clause, so 'before you eat' is both the closer rendering and the one that picks this sentence out.

standard: reality (the everyday borrowing)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). реа́льность is the everyday borrowing; действи́тельность the native, bookish word.

en: The shirt has lost a button.
note: «У руба́шки» is the possessive у + genitive frame, which English renders with the shirt as subject; «На руба́шке» keeps the button as subject. Saying so separates the two and teaches the frame.

en: Wash your hands before the meal.
note: One of three sentences sharing 'Wash your hands before eating'. «пе́ред едо́й» is a noun phrase, so 'before the meal' renders it and leaves the general instruction to мыть's imperfective.

standard: market (the standard word; also the market in economics)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). ры́нок is the standard word, and the one economics uses; база́р is the open-air bazaar.

en: Turn off to the right at the shop.
note: Shared a prompt with поверну́ть's identical sentence. сверну́ть is turning off the road you are on, which English says with 'turn off'.

standard: to become (colloquial, of a state that comes on)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). сде́латься is colloquial, of a state that comes on; стать is the everyday word.

en: The table stands in the centre of the room.
note: посреди́ is a preposition, which the hint builder never uses, so its sentence could never be told from this one. середи́на is as much 'centre' as 'middle', and that carries the difference.

standard: soon (the everyday word, a short time from now)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). ско́ро is the everyday word, measured from now; вско́ре is bookish and measured from another event.

A near-clone of шу́тка's «Он рассказа́л смешну́ю шу́тку», with the whole difference carried by анекдо́т — a gloss-only stub, not a taught word — while the hint drew on смешно́й in both. The adjective gets its own masculine-accusative sentence instead; the annotation still points at token 3.

standard: to become (the everyday word, gradually turning into)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). станови́ться is the everyday word for gradually turning into something; де́латься is colloquial.

standard: to become (the everyday word; also to start, or to stand)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). стать is the everyday word; сде́латься is the colloquial one. The existing 'to start; to stand' senses are kept — they are the rest of what стать does.

standard: creative (the native word, used of art and artistic work)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). тво́рческий is the native word, tied to тво́рчество and to artistic work; креати́вный is the recent borrowing.

ru_new: Подожди́ меня́ тут, я сейча́с верну́сь.
en: Wait for me here, I'll be right back.
note: A word-for-word clone of здесь's sentence. тут is filed as a particle, which the hint builder never uses, so only the sentence could carry the difference.

standard: extremely (formal and bookish, exceedingly)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). чрезвыча́йно is formal and bookish; кра́йне is the everyday intensifier.
A clone of сия́ть's «Со́лнце я́рко сия́ет», and свети́ть's own hint came from a glossary stub with no note. A lamp is what свети́ть is prototypically about, and я́рко is taught either way.

standard: clearly (evident, plain to see; also of a cloudless sky)
note: Both members of a colliding English prompt were glossed as paraphrases of each other, so the generated hint named no distinction the learner could act on (#601). я́сно is what is evident in itself — and the word for a cloudless sky; поня́тно is what has been understood.
